simple.meaning: בְּעֵרָה (bᵉʻêrâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a burning.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Exodus, beginning at Exodus 22:5. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּעֵרָה (H1200) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בְּעֵרָה (bᵉʻêrâh) / H1200 is traced through Exodus 22:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten by letting his animal loose, and it grazes in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.
